input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) makes Customer's convenience termination conditional on paying "early termination charges" whose amount is left entirely to Attachment A and the Service Option Attachments (no Attachment A charge schedule appears in the document), and Section 3.3 confirms those charges are recoverable by IBM except where IBM is the breaching party. That is an uncapped, Customer-payable liquidated amount, which fails the fallback requirement of an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount. We therefore adopted the fallback: a cap of three months' charges for the terminated Services, expressed as the sole liquidated amount payable by us, rather than deleting the charge outright (which would leave the Section 3.3 cross-reference dangling). The late payment fees referenced in Section 4.2 are a payment-timing charge rather than a liquidated damages regime and are noted only for completeness.

ops.text: Any early termination charges payable by Customer under Section 3.4(b) will not exceed three months' charges for the terminated Services and are the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay no liquidated damages; as a fallback we accept an early-termination fee capped at three months' charges, so we have capped the Section 3.4(b) charges at that level and made them the sole liquidated amount payable by us.
proposal.summary: Cap Section 3.4(b) early termination charges at three months' charges as the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.

mappings.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
